guidelines.detail: same as LRN-008 (The description states that an employee or customer reports an incident to begin the process. The reference has a distinct task for that action before logging, while the generated model uses a start event for it instead. This is the situation addressed by LRN-008.)

same as LRN-007 (The description states the completion outcome, follow-up purpose, and solution options, while the paired reference labels omit some of those details. The proposed guidance is already covered by LRN-007; the other label pairs are largely faithful paraphrases.)

same as LRN-008 (The description states that an employee or customer reports an incident to begin the process, while the records show the start-to-report and report-to-logging flows are absent. This guideline matches the learned rule LRN-008.)

same as LRN-020 (The generated labels retain described purpose, outcome, and alternatives that the reference labels omit or narrow. The description supports preserving those details; this guideline is already essentially stated by learned guideline LRN-020.)

same as LRN-017 (The description identifies alternative ways to implement the solution, and the records show the reference models separate activities and choice gateways for alternatives that are absent from the generated model. This is already captured by learned guideline LRN-017.)

refines FID-03 (The description allows multiple forms of implementation, while the reference label selects only one. A general label preserves the described alternatives; this refines the documented guidance to use short, faithful labels.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that a participant performs an action that initiates the process: Model the process trigger with a start event, then model the participant’s described action as a distinct task; do not use the action itself as the start event.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that a participant performs an action that initiates the process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description distinguishes a process trigger, an activity, or an outcome from other stages of the process: Label each BPMN element according to the meaning of its corresponding described trigger, activity, or outcome; do not substitute a different stage or its purpose or result.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states a specific activity purpose, meaningful qualifier, or completion outcome for a BPMN element

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description distinguishes an event or activity by its action, actor, object, recipient, or another meaningful qualifier: Label each BPMN element so that it preserves those stated details without substituting a broader or different meaning.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states an activity or outcome together with its purpose, result, or alternative forms

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description presents two or more distinct activities as alternatives: Model each activity as a separate task on its own branch rather than combining the alternatives into one task; choose a gateway that matches whether one or multiple alternatives may be performed.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description presents two or more distinct activities as alternative ways to achieve an outcome

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description presents multiple alternative ways to perform one activity: Label the BPMN activity at a level of generality that preserves the alternatives rather than selecting only one.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description presents multiple alternative ways to perform one activity
